question.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y=16\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(x)=A{e}^{-2x}+Bx{e}^{-2x}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y=16\operatorname{sin}⁡2x,\,y(0)=-1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=-2.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We find the constants $A$ and $B$ by substituting the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(0)=-1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =A{e}^{-2(0)}+B(0){e}^{-2(0)}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2(0) \\ -1 & =A-2 \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Differentiating $y$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=-2A{e}^{-2x}-2Bx{e}^{-2x}+B{e}^{-2x}+4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=-2$ into the derivative gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =-2A{e}^{-2(0)}-2B(0){e}^{-2(0)}+B{e}^{-2(0)}+4\operatorname{sin}⁡2(0) \\ -2 & =-2A+B \\ -2 & =-2+B \\ B & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $A=1$ and $B=0,$ we have the following solution to the initial value problem:

$$
y={e}^{-2x}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$
